turns.input: Orla Fen gives Nicco a pair of leather boots.
turns.narration:
Orla Fen stood in Heartstone Square, a cloth bundle tucked under one arm and her free hand pushing back strands of grey hair that the wind had loosened. She held the worn leather boots she'd brought from the shop, turning them over to inspect the soles with a critical eye.

"You look new around the tower," she said, meeting his gaze with the directness of someone who spoke over laundry noise for a living. She made no move to extend them. "These came out of the pile left by whoever cleared out. Good enough leather, still. If you want them, say so—I'm not standing here as a display stand."

narration_reconciliation.draft:
Orla Fen already stood in Heartstone Square, a cloth bundle tucked under one arm and her free hand pushing back strands of grey hair that the wind had loosened. She recognized the tall, unfamiliar man by the plainness of his clothes rather than any face she knew—new to the tower, or new to the neighborhood, or both. Before he could speak, she held out the worn leather boots she'd brought from the shop.

"You're the one they say took Heartstone," she said, not quite a question. "These came out of the pile left by the last lot. Good enough leather, still. Take them or don't—I'm not carrying them back to the Basin just to store grime in my shelves."

She kept her hand extended, waiting, her reddened forearms and the thick waterproofed apron marking her well enough for anyone who'd ever needed sheets washed in a hurry.

turns.input:
Thanks *he said to them, after which he decides to give them back the boots*
You'll need them more than me
turns.narration:
Orla Fen's heavy forearms tense as Nicco speaks. She takes back the boots without ceremony, her reddened hands closing around the leather without looking down. "I gave them already washed," she says, her voice carrying that laundry-hall volume even in the open square. "You keep tramping through the streets in whatevers, you'll understand fast enough." She doesn't ask why he refused; her jaw sets briefly, more puzzled than offended.

She hooks the boots onto a belt loop with a practiced motion, already turning toward The Coined Lie or her own route home. "Laundry's water and soap, not charity." The words follow her movement, neither lingering nor hurrying. "You change your mind, you know where the basin sits."
